literal: That autumn, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Jingshan Commandery.
idiomatic: That autumn he was raised to Prince of Jingshan Commandery.

literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Guang was executed; an edict dispatched Central Palace Army Commander Helba Fu'en and more than ten others by post-horse relay to seize Xian.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, after Guang was put to death, an edict sent Central Palace Army Commander Helba Fu'en and a dozen others by relay horse to seize Xian.

literal: Campaign Commander Grand General Xianyu Taozhi and Luozhou Circuit Executive Assistant Master of Writing Dugu Yongye were ordered to mobilize at once the cavalry of Ding Province as reinforcements; Yongye was to replace Xian.
idiomatic: Campaign commander Grand General Xianyu Taozhi and Luozhou circuit executive assistant Dugu Yongye were ordered to mobilize Ding Province cavalry at once as reinforcements, and Yongye was to replace Xian in office.

literal: When Fu'en and the rest arrived, the gatekeepers reported that the envoys wore hidden armor and their horses were lathered with sweat — the city gates ought to be shut.
idiomatic: When Fu'en and his men arrived, the gatekeepers reported that the envoys wore armor beneath their robes and their horses ran wet with sweat — the city gates ought to be barred.

literal: Xian said: "How can an imperial envoy be met with suspicion and refusal?
idiomatic: Xian said, "How can one meet an imperial envoy with suspicion and turn him away?

literal: " He went out to receive them; Fu'en took him by the hand, seized him, and he died in the chief administrator's hall.
idiomatic: " He went out to receive them. Fu'en took his hand — and seized him. He died in the chief administrator's hall.

literal: At the end he sighed: "Wealth and honor such as this — a daughter queen, princesses filling the house, always keeping three hundred armed retainers — how could we not fall?
idiomatic: At the end he sighed: "Wealth and honor such as this — a daughter made queen, princesses in every corner of the house, three hundred armed retainers always at call — how could we not fall?

literal: " And his five sons Shida, Shiqian, Shibian, Shiyou, and Fuhu were executed; those aged fifteen or under were spared.
idiomatic: " His five sons Shida, Shiqian, Shibian, Shiyou, and Fuhu were put to death; those fifteen or younger were spared.

literal: Before Xian was executed, he suddenly had five or six of his sons then in the province — from Fuhu downward — led out of the city with chains around their necks, riding donkeys; the whole household wept and escorted them to the gate, then returned as evening fell.
idiomatic: Before Xian was executed, he suddenly had five or six sons then in the province — from Fuhu on down — led out of the city with chains at their throats, riding donkeys. The whole household wept and escorted them to the gate, then returned as evening fell.

literal: Officials and common people alike were startled and dismayed.
idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were struck with wonder and dread.

literal: Yan Commandery acting magistrate Ma Siming — a man skilled in medicine, whom Xian admired — privately asked him what it meant. Xian answered: "We need a rite to avert ill fortune.
idiomatic: Ma Siming, acting magistrate of Yan Commandery — a physician Xian held in esteem — privately asked what it meant. Xian answered, "We need a rite to turn aside ill fortune.

literal: " Within days this calamity came.
idiomatic: " Within days the calamity arrived.

literal: Both Xian and Guang mastered riding and archery in youth; their father each day sent them out to hunt, and on their return compared what game each had taken.
idiomatic: Both Xian and Guang were skilled in riding and archery from youth. Each day their father sent them out to hunt; on their return he compared the game each had taken.

literal: If Guang's bag was small, he always placed his arrow through the turtle's shell and clear through to the armpit.
idiomatic: If Guang's bag was light, he always drove his arrow through the turtle's shell and out beneath the armpit.

literal: Xian might take more, but not in the vital places.
idiomatic: Xian might take more, but never in the vital places.

literal: Guang was often rewarded; Xian was sometimes beaten with the rod.
idiomatic: Guang was often praised and rewarded; Xian was sometimes beaten with the rod.

literal: When people asked why, Jin answered: "Mingyue always plants his arrow in the beast's back; Fengle strikes wherever he can — though the count may be greater, he falls far short of his elder brother.
idiomatic: When people asked why, Jin answered: "Mingyue always plants his arrow in the beast's back. Fengle strikes wherever he can — though the count may be greater, he falls far short of his elder brother.

literal: " All who heard were convinced by his words.
idiomatic: " All who heard were convinced.

literal: Jin's elder brother Ping was skilled with bow and horse and possessed practical ability.
idiomatic: Jin's elder brother Ping was skilled with bow and horse and had real capacity for command.

literal: During the Jingming era of Wei he entered service as a palace guard general and was transferred to Xiangwei General.
idiomatic: In the Jingming era of Wei he entered service as a palace guard general and was transferred to Xiangwei General.

literal: At the end of Zhengguang, when the six garrisons rose in turmoil, he served under Grand General Yu Bin on the northern campaign.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang, when the six garrisons fell into turmoil, he served under Grand General Yu Bin on the northern campaign.

literal: The army was defeated and he was captured by the rebels.
idiomatic: The army was defeated and he was taken by the rebels.

literal: Later he fled to join his brother Jin at Yunzhou and was advanced to rank as Dragon-Tiger General.
idiomatic: Later he fled to his brother Jin at Yunzhou and was advanced to Dragon-Tiger General.

literal: With Jin he led their following south; at Huangguadui they were routed by Du Luozhou and their tribes scattered.
idiomatic: With Jin he led their following south. At Huangguadui they were broken by Du Luozhou and their tribes scattered.

literal: When they returned to Erzhu Rong, he was treated with great favor, and Ping inherited their father's title as First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples.
idiomatic: When they returned to Erzhu Rong, he was treated with great favor, and Ping inherited their father's title as First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples.

literal: The historian writes: Hulü Jin, at the outset when Gao Huan was settling the chaos, helped establish the royal enterprise; his loyalty was complete, and so this great achievement was won — thus he lived out his years in full and stood above all the hundred ministers.
idiomatic: The historian writes: Hulü Jin, at the outset when Gao Huan was settling the chaos, helped establish the royal enterprise. His loyalty was complete, and so this great achievement was won — thus he lived out his years in full and stood above all the hundred ministers.

literal: Yet see how the warning against overflowing fullness moves in small ways: it had scarcely touched the next generation when execution and extermination followed — though the weight of power was great, it still matched what the Daoist masters warn against.
idiomatic: Yet see how the warning against overflowing fullness moves in small ways: it had scarcely touched the next generation when execution and extermination followed. Though the weight of power was great, it still matched what the Daoist masters warn against.

literal: Guang, as the son of a supreme general, bore a grave and resolute bearing; in tactical craft and military command he matched hidden stratagem — facing the enemy he seized victory, shifting without fixed form.
idiomatic: Guang, as the son of a supreme general, bore a grave and resolute bearing. In tactical craft and military command he matched hidden stratagem — facing the enemy he seized victory, shifting without fixed form.

literal: Since the passes and the Yellow River divided the realm, nearly four decades had passed.
idiomatic: Since the passes and the Yellow River divided the realm, nearly four decades had passed.

literal: At the height of Gao Huan's hegemony, in the very days when the Yuwen clan was first founding its state, their armies went forth on punitive raids and again and again blunted the enemy's edge.
idiomatic: At the height of Gao Huan's hegemony, in the very days when the Yuwen clan was first founding its state, their armies went forth on punitive raids and again and again blunted the enemy's edge.

literal: But from the Daning era onward, the eastern neighbor weakened by degrees; in the west they first took Bashu, then destroyed Jiangling — the tide ran downhill for war, and the spirit of annexation gathered strength.
idiomatic: But from the Daning era onward, the eastern neighbor weakened by degrees. In the west they first took Bashu, then destroyed Jiangling — the tide ran downhill for war, and the spirit of annexation gathered strength.

literal: The Hulü clan disciplined the army, rallied the host, and held the border fast — in battle no enemy line stood whole; in siege scarcely a city held intact. Qi could always bring the foe to bay; Qin no longer had a plan to force the passes open.
idiomatic: The Hulü clan disciplined the army, rallied the host, and held the border fast — in battle no enemy line stood whole; in siege scarcely a city held intact. Qi could always bring the foe to bay; Qin no longer had a plan to force the passes open.

literal: Yet in an age of disorder, talent itself became a triumph — and fraud clothed itself in the majesty that overawes a ruler.
idiomatic: Yet in an age of disorder, talent itself became a triumph — and fraud clothed itself in the majesty that overawes a ruler.

literal: The ruler was dim, the times were hard, and the realm tore down its own ramparts.
idiomatic: The ruler was dim, the times were hard, and the realm tore down its own ramparts.

literal: Long ago, when Li Mu served Zhao as general, he cut down the northern raiders and drove back the armies of Qin — Guo Kai slandered him; Li Mu died, and Zhao was destroyed.
idiomatic: Long ago, when Li Mu served Zhao as general, he cut down the northern raiders and drove back the armies of Qin. Guo Kai slandered him; Li Mu died, and Zhao was destroyed.

literal: Were those who counseled Guang's death perhaps Qin's agents of division? Same craft, same ruin!
idiomatic: Were those who counseled Guang's death perhaps Qin's agents of division? Same craft, same ruin!

literal: Within, they had the generals disband; without, they repaid a powerful neighbor's grudge.
idiomatic: Within, they had the generals disband; without, they repaid a powerful neighbor's grudge.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: Men of later times — let this be a warning deeply taken.
idiomatic: Men of later times — let this be a warning deeply taken.

literal: The encomium says: Steadfast Xianyang — the brilliance of clan and state.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Steadfast Xianyang — brilliance of clan and state.

literal: Mingyue, loyal and mighty — general and minister through generations.
idiomatic: Mingyue, loyal and mighty — general and minister through generations.

literal: His fame shook the lands west of the passes; his stature outran the regard of his age.
idiomatic: His fame shook the lands west of the passes; his stature outran the regard of his age.

literal: Pressed by such renown, slander easily rose.
idiomatic: Pressed by such renown, slander easily rose.

literal: It began with clever speech — and ended in mutual ruin.
idiomatic: It began with clever speech — and ended in mutual ruin.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
